title: Schema-aware streaming fallback and tool-call safety acceptance
creator: Ava Liu
description: Clarify and accept minimal requirements for structured output streaming and function/tool calls when partial objects, truncated streams, and runtime errors occur. This ticket defines the acceptance criteria, tests, and rollout plan for schema-aware fallbacks, deterministic retry semantics for tool invocations, backpressure/resume semantics for progressive emission, and observability signals required to diagnose regressions.
background: Multiple PM and ENG tickets identified classes of failures when models stream partial JSON objects or emit an unexpected field ordering during tool handoff. Customers have built orchestration on top of tool calls and need deterministic guarantees for idempotency and resume semantics. The runtime historically applied simple fallback to plaintext or closed the connection; this work specifies acceptable behavior for production applications and ties to telemetry and test harnesses.
scope: This ticket covers acceptance criteria for: 1) streaming JSON fragments with checkpointed resume tokens, 2) graceful fallbacks when schema validation fails mid-stream, 3) explicit tool-call handshake semantics including idempotency keys and retry windows, and 4) observability events and metrics used to validate correctness. It includes test cases and rollout guidance. Implementation details (kernels, batching internals) are out of scope.
out_of_scope: Model-level generation quality tuning, kernel selection, per-GPU batching policy changes, SDK surface changes beyond metadata headers, and enterprise-only connectivity modes (on-prem packaging) for this iteration.
success_metrics: Decrease in 'partial-emit' customer complaints by 90% within 8 weeks of release
0 known SEV incidents caused by tool-call race conditions in first 30 days
Observability coverage: 100% of streaming calls emit checksum/resume tokens and schema-validation events
Automated test harness: >=95% pass rate on randomized fragment reordering and backpressure tests
acceptance_criteria: API emits a streaming envelope that contains: frame_type, sequence_number, optional resume_token, and canonical_schema_id when emitting structured fragments

When a schema validation error occurs mid-stream the service must: 1) emit an explicit 'schema_error' frame with error_code and best-effort partial_serialized_prefix, 2) include a resume_token when available, and 3) leave connection open to allow client-directed repair or abort
Tool/function invocation must include an idempotency_key header generated by the platform; retries with the same key are deduplicated server-side for a configurable retry window (default 60s)

If a tool call is accepted but the downstream tool fails with a retryable error, runtime must return a structured 'tool_retry' frame containing suggested_retry_after_ms and diagnostic_reason; automatic retries are only performed when policy set to 'auto-retry'

Backpressure: client-sent 'REQ_PAUSE' and server-sent 'SLOWDOWN' frames are honored; server will buffer at most N frames (configurable) before emitting 'backpressure_drop' events if client doesn't resume

Resume semantics: clients may reconnect with resume_token within 300s and must receive remaining fragments in canonical order; if resume_token expired runtime returns a 'resume_expired' terminal frame and a best-effort synthetic reconciliation summary

Partial-object policy: runtime must never emit malformed JSON as final successful response; if final emission contains structural violations, the call is marked 'invalidated' and a non-2xx status and structured failure payload is returned

Observability: every streaming call and tool invocation must emit structured telemetry events (call_start, frame_emit, schema_validation_result, tool_handshake, tool_terminal) with trace_id and sampleable payload hashes
Compatibility: clients without streaming support must be able to opt into a non-streaming fallback that receives the reconciled final object and a schema_compatibility flag
test_plan: Unit tests: validate envelope framing (sequence_number and resume_token) under simulated network fragment reordering
Property tests: fuzz JSON fragment emission and assert that resume and reconciliation produce identical canonical object as uninterrupted emission
Integration: simulate flaky downstream tool that returns transient 502 and permanent 400; verify idempotency_key dedup and 'tool_retry' frames behavior
Load test: exercise backpressure by generating 50K concurrent long-lived streams and ensure backpressure_drop rate <0.1%
E2E: use harness runner to reconnect with stale resume_token and assert 'resume_expired' behavior and reconciliation summary correctness
Acceptance lab: QA runs manual scenarios with sample client SDK to confirm non-streaming fallback receives reconciled object and schema_compatibility flag
rollout_plan: Canary: enable schema-aware streaming for 5% of production traffic for 48 hours; monitor error rates and schema_error frame volume
Ramp: 25% for 48 hours, 50% for 24 hours, then global if SLOs stable
Kill-switch: server-side gate to disable streaming envelope and fall back to legacy behavior within 10 minutes
Post-rollout: 2-week observational window with daily runbook review and customer outreach to early adopters
observability_requirements: All frames must include trace_id and sequence_number for downstream correlation
Emit histograms for time-to-first-frame and time-between-frames; alert if p95 > configured latency SLO
Schema validation metrics: counts of valid, soft_failure (recoverable), hard_failure (invalidate call), and corrected_via_reconciliation
Tool-call telemetry: handshake_latency_ms, downstream_status_code, dedup_hit (boolean), retry_count
SLO dashboards and an on-call alert when partial-emits leading to invalidated calls exceed threshold
observability_playbook_notes: If 'schema_error' frames spike, capture sample traces and raw frame payloads and link to PRD for triage
Use reruns in the harness with the failing seeds to reproduce nondeterministic failures
If dedup_hit is low but retry_count high, investigate idempotency_key propagation in SDKs and proxies
owner_responsibilities: PM: finalize acceptance language and run QA sign-off
ENG: implement envelope headers, dedup store for idempotency keys, and resume token lifecycle
SRE: create dashboards, alerts, and the canary gating controls
DX/SDK: ensure client headers and resume semantics are documented and example code provided
notes: Design trade-off considered: embedding full canonical_schema in each frame vs canonical_schema_id + registry lookup. Chosen: canonical_schema_id to reduce bandwidth and allow schema evolution via registry versioning
Resume token design: token encodes (call_id, last_sequence_number, checksum) and is HMAC-signed to prevent tampering
Idempotency store uses bounded LRU with TTL aligned to retry window to limit memory overhead
